record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.original_question: Let α_r(Γ) be the maximum size of an r-independent set in a continuous graph Γ, where an r-independent set is a subset I ⊆ E whose distinct points are pairwise at distance at least 2r. For a rational radius r > 0, does there exist a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for the maximum r-independent set problem whose approximation ratio is bounded below by an absolute constant that does not depend on the input size?

evidence.quote: Definition 9. Given a positive real number r > 0, a set of points I ⊆ E is called an r-independent (or r-stable) set of Γ if for any two points p, q ∈ I, it holds that d(p, q) ≥ 2r. The r-independence number of Γ, further referred as αr(Γ) or αr for simplicity, is the cardinality of the maximum r-independent set in Γ.

The specific open question we ask in this paragraph reads: For any rational number r > 0, is there a polynomial time approximation algorithm for the maximum r-independent set problem with performance guarantee bounded by a constant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a continuous graph Γ as the topological space obtained from a finite simple graph G = (V,E_G) by replacing each edge uv ∈ E_G with a homeomorphic copy of the closed unit interval [0,1], glued at endpoints according to V; let E denote the resulting underlying point set (the union of all edge-intervals together with the vertices). Equip E with the intrinsic shortest-path metric d in which each edge has length 1, so that d(p,q) is the length of a shortest path inside E from p to q.

For a real number r > 0, call a subset I ⊆ E an r-independent set of Γ if d(p,q) ≥ 2r for every pair of distinct points p,q ∈ I. Define the r-independence number
   α_r(Γ) := sup{ |I| : I ⊆ E is r-independent }.
(For each fixed rational r > 0, α_r(Γ) is finite for every finite continuous graph Γ.)

The maximum r-independent set problem takes as input a finite continuous graph Γ (specified, e.g., by its underlying combinatorial graph G together with the rational number r) and asks for an r-independent set of maximum cardinality.

Question: Fix a rational number r > 0. Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm A and an absolute constant c = c(r) > 0 (independent of the input size) such that, on every input continuous graph Γ, A outputs an r-independent set I_A of Γ with
   |I_A| ≥ c · α_r(Γ) ?

Equivalently, does the maximum r-independent set problem on continuous graphs admit a constant-factor polynomial-time approximation algorithm?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up any polynomial-time constant-factor approximation algorithm for the maximum r-independent set problem on continuous (metric) graphs for arbitrary rational r > 0. Related results exist for unit disk graphs and intersection graphs, but they do not resolve the question for general continuous graphs. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs (arXiv:2501.14554)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey introducing continuous graphs (each edge a unit-length interval) and discussing combinatorial parameters such as the r-independence number α_r(Γ).
status_evidence.claim: The survey explicitly poses as an open question whether a constant-factor polynomial-time approximation exists for the maximum r-independent set problem on continuous graphs.

status_evidence.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Independent Set on Unit Disk Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: PTAS-style results for maximum independent set on geometric/unit-disk graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existing constant-factor and PTAS approximation results address geometric graph classes but do not directly resolve the r-independent set question on continuous graphs.
